items.title: Bargain hunters have a new shopping destination near Mississauga
items.summary: A new discount shopping destination has opened near Mississauga, giving bargain hunters another place to look for deals on everything from household essentials to brand-name merchandise. Clearance Warehouse officially opened its newest location on Thursday (Nov. 5) at 2307 Royal Windsor Drive in Oakville, near the intersection of Ford Drive and just west of the Mississauga border. The roughly 30,000-square-foot warehouse has taken over the former RONA building and is offering a wide selection of liquidation, overstock and clearance merchandise, with advertised discounts ranging from 30 to 90 per cent off regular retail prices. Shoppers can expect to find a changing assortment of goods, including housewares, kitchen products, small appliances, bedding, health and beauty products, cleaning supplies, hardware, tools and seasonal merchandise. The selection is expected to change regularly as new merchandise arrives and existing stock sells out, meaning shoppers may find different products on subsequent visits. The Oakville location is the latest addition to Clearance Warehouse’s GTA operations. The company also has locations in Brampton and Etobicoke, both of which opened for the current sale period in October. The Brampton store is located at 10 Bramhurst Avenue, while the Etobicoke location can be found at 375 Queens Plate Drive. The warehouse sale concept operates for a limited time rather than as a traditional year-round retail store. The current sale period at all three locations is scheduled to run until December 24.

items.title: 4,100 tonnes less salt will be used on Mississauga roads during winter: city
items.summary: Mississauga plans to significantly cut its road salt use this winter to better protect the environment and infrastructure while still keeping drivers safe. City of Mississauga officials said this week they’re taking recent salt-reduction efforts to another level in the months and years ahead. They expect to cut road salt use by as much as 4,100 tonnes annually. “In 2026, the city will expand the use of anti-icing brine (liquid mix of water and salt) to 20 per cent more roads. This is expected to reduce salt use by up to 650 tonnes a year,” the city said, adding it will also “start plowing snow earlier on select major roads, which could bring down salt use by 3,450 tonnes a year. ” The program currently covers approximately 1,260 lane kilometres of roadway, “which is about 63,000 litres of salt brine for each application,” city officials continued. ” Last fall, as the 2025-26 winter loomed, Mississauga Ward 1 Coun.

items.title: Longtime Metro grocery store closes after decades in Mississauga
items.summary: A Mississauga grocery store with decades of history has closed its doors, marking the end of an era for a neighbourhood shopping destination that has operated under several different names. The Metro grocery store at 406 Lakeshore Road East, in the Lakeshore Plaza shopping centre near Cawthra Road in the Lakeview neighbourhood, shut down on Nov. 4. But the closure will lead to a new beginning. The familiar supermarket is being converted into a Food Basics, with the new discount grocery store expected to open sometime in the new year. READ MORE: New discount grocery store opens in Toronto The location has a long history serving Mississauga shoppers, having operated over the years as Miracle Food Mart, Dominion and, most recently, Metro. For generations of residents, the store has been a familiar part of the neighbourhood, surviving changes in ownership and grocery store branding while continuing to serve local shoppers. , which operates both the Metro and Food Basics grocery banners. The company has been converting a number of its traditional Metro locations into discount Food Basics stores as shoppers increasingly look for ways to save on groceries. The change will bring a different shopping format to the Lakeshore Plaza location, although it will remain under the same corporate ownership.

items.title: Former seniors’ apartment buildings transformed after controversial eviction in Mississauga
items.summary: Former seniors’ apartment buildings, once subject to a controversial eviction, have been completely transformed in Mississauga. A newly revitalized rental apartment community at 6509 and 6521 Glen Erin Dr. in Meadowvale is now complete. Minto held a launch event with a ribbon-cutting last month. items.title: Streetsville's Hyde Mill Ruins to Be Preserved as Three Unsafe Structures Come Down
items.summary: Three deteriorating structures at Mississauga's Hyde Mill Ruins are being torn down over safety concerns, the city says, as crews prepare to restore the historic Streetsville site. According to Ward 11 Councillor Brad Butt, the demolition targets buildings on the site, which sits on the banks of the Credit River at the foot of Ontario Street and dates back to the early 1840s, while the ruins themselves will be protected during construction and preserved in place. Butt said demolition and initial site restoration work took place in September and October. Planting and seeding are scheduled to begin next week, followed by backfilling and further landscape restoration, he said. The councillor added that temporary construction and demolition noise will continue in the area over the coming weeks.

items.title: Mississauga Reminds Residents of New Fireworks Bylaw as Diwali Celebrations Begin
items.summary: The City of Mississauga is reminding residents to follow its newer fireworks bylaw as Diwali celebrations run from Nov. 6 to 10, with the main day falling on Sunday, Nov. 8. According to the city, family and backyard fireworks can be set off without a permit on private property only on Nov. 8, while a permit is required to use them on any other day or to hold a display in a city park or other public space. Officials said fireworks are never allowed on roads, sidewalks, in parking lots or elsewhere on public property. The city said it is adding extra bylaw enforcement officers this year after receiving a record 432 complaints about Diwali fireworks during the 2025 festival. Residents were also reminded not to call 911 over fireworks unless there is immediate danger, such as a fire or injury, and to instead report illegal fireworks through the city's 311 line or website.

items.title: Jackknifed Truck Shuts Down All Express Lanes on Highway 401 in Mississauga
items.summary: All express lanes on Highway 401 in Mississauga were shut down Friday morning after a crash involving a jackknifed truck, according to the Ministry of Transportation's 511 traffic site. The Ontario Provincial Police confirmed the express lanes were closed while crews responded to the scene. Ministry of Transportation photos showed the jackknifed truck surrounded by emergency vehicles as crews worked to clear the wreckage. Police advised drivers to expect delays if travelling through the area and urged them to plan alternate routes where possible. Traffic backed up significantly in the express lanes as the cleanup continued into the morning.

items.title: Peel Police Data Shows 332 Vehicles Stolen in Mississauga Over Two Months, Clustered Near Square One and Pearson
items.summary: Peel Regional Police data shows 332 vehicles were reported stolen in Mississauga between Sept. 1 and Oct. 31, averaging more than six thefts a day across the two-month span. According to the force's online crime-mapping tool, the thefts were not evenly spread across the city, with notable clusters forming around Square One and Pearson International Airport. The interactive map, available on the Peel Regional Police website, plots the approximate location of each reported theft. Police noted that some points on the map may represent more than one vehicle stolen in the same area. The tool allows residents to see where auto thefts have been concentrated in recent months across the region.
